title: Personal Checking: conditions besides the balance test for a conversion to Private Client Checking
content:
## Scope

This rule applies when the owner of an active Personal Checking account asks to convert it to Private Client Checking. Besides the Relationship Balance part of the Private Client entry gate, the conditions of the general tier conversion rules continue to apply unchanged.

## Formal clause

The other conditions of the general Personal Checking tier conversion rules are inherited unchanged and must also hold:

1. the account is active;
2. the owner's age is at least Private Client Checking's youngest age to open;
3. the owner holds fewer Private Client Checking accounts than that tier's maximum per customer, and stays within the overall Personal Checking account-holding cap; and
4. no other customer-requested conversion has been recorded on the account in the current statement cycle.

Where any of them fails, no conversion is written, whatever the Relationship Balance.

**How the once-per-cycle limit is judged.** The checking records keep no dated history of conversions apart from the account's current tier, so the once-per-cycle limit is judged on the conversions recorded during the current contact together with any the owner reports having made earlier in the cycle; when neither shows one, the limit holds.

## Checklist

| Condition | Read from | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Account active | The account record | No conversion |
| Owner's age at least Private Client Checking's youngest age to open | Date of birth on the customer profile | No conversion |
| Fewer Private Client Checking accounts than the tier maximum, and within the overall cap | The customer's accounts on record | No conversion |
| No other customer-requested conversion on the account this statement cycle | Conversions recorded during the current contact, and any the owner reports having made earlier in the cycle | No conversion |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- **Dormant account.** An owner whose account is dormant asks for the conversion. The account is not active, so no conversion is written, even if the owner's balances are far above any Private Client requirement.
- **Earlier conversion reported by the owner.** The owner says the account was converted from Everyday Checking to Interest Checking earlier in the current statement cycle and now asks for Private Client Checking. That reported conversion counts, so the once-per-cycle limit fails and no conversion is written.
- **Nothing recorded, nothing reported.** No conversion has been recorded during the current contact and the owner reports none earlier in the cycle. The once-per-cycle limit holds.
- **Two requests in one contact.** A conversion was already recorded earlier in the same contact. It counts toward the limit, so a second customer-requested conversion in this cycle is not written.
- **Tier maximum.** The owner already holds as many Private Client Checking accounts as that tier allows per customer. No conversion is written.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "a high enough Relationship Balance overrides the other conditions". **Correct basis:** where any inherited condition fails, no conversion is written whatever the Relationship Balance.
